definitions.meaning: a village green is ... land shared by all

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the colour green is hardly a rare choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A common is an open public ground like a green, and common also means ordinary or everyday.

indicators.note: originally says take the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a team ahead is up, as in one up
a draw is a tie

explanation.surface: A team that first charged forward then settled for a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a knockout match in a cup competition such as the FA Cup in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup tie is a single match, or game, in a knockout cup competition.

clue.text: Drink in vermouth sheepish male served up

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the pieces are written bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A drink with vermouth served by a shy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses IN + IT + RAM in this down clue. 'sheepish' means of sheep, not shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth.

indicators.note: having some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deity who means well.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology.

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A national song that a particular man wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' suits the music of the surface but signals that THE MAN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A national anthem is the patriotic song a country sings on formal occasions.

definitions.meaning: the polite reply to thanks, meaning it was no trouble
an emphatic denial, meaning in no way

explanation.surface: A gracious reply to thanks paired with a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a courteous answer to thanks and an emphatic way to say no.

clue.text: Ben riding chariot over great lake

parts.note: Ben-Hur is the chariot-racing hero of the novel and film, so the name after Ben is Hur
on means over, as in on top of

explanation.surface: A chariot-riding hero passes over one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Huron is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday
key means crucial or important

explanation.surface: A big day for an ape or monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkeys belong to the primate order of mammals, along with apes and humans.

clue.text: Couple I snubbed, one of fifty in the US

definitions.text: one of fifty in the US

parts.note: to couple is to connect or join
to cut someone is to snub them, ignoring them deliberately

explanation.surface: Someone joined to a partner feels cold-shouldered in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a pair of people but is the verb, meaning join.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is one of the fifty states that make up the US.

clue.text: Covered entrance I start to construct in Iberian city

indicators.note: in says the preceding pieces go inside the city's name

parts.note: Porto is the Portuguese city on the Iberian peninsula

indicators.note: start to says take only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone plans to build a sheltered doorway in a Portuguese city.
explanation.walkthrough: Porto is often called Oporto in English; 'start to' takes only the first letter of 'construct'.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch with a roof held up by columns at a building's entrance.

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to wind a road or a handle is to turn it
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A windy European city where the breeze eats up a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as breeze but is the verb, as in winding a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city of northern Italy, in Europe.

clue.text: Plant in rather isolated situation, initially

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A plant growing somewhere fairly remote.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a flowering garden plant with sword-shaped leaves.

parts.note: something fashionable is in
a stance is a point of view or attitude

explanation.surface: A trendy outlook offered up as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' looks like one phrase, but 'for' is a link and 'example' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or illustration of something.

parts.note: a stand is a position taken, as on an issue
Rd is the usual written short form of road, as in street addresses

explanation.surface: The usual place for something to sit is on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means usual or ordinary, the accepted norm.

parts.note: a rib is a bone of the chest
tickling is light touching of the skin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny bone' reads as the elbow nerve, but 'Funny' is the definition and 'bone' the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rib-tickling is very amusing, enough to make you laugh hard.

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so the gallery name is put inside the sign word

parts.note: a nod is a sign of agreement
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery's arrival is marked by a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE goes into NOD: NO TATE D.
explanation.definitionFit: Notated means written down in symbols, such as music marked on a stave.

indicators.note: about means around, so the bet word goes around the other

parts.note: a bet is a speculation or gamble
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Gossip about everyone at the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: BET goes 'about' ALL: B ALL ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is a classical form of theatrical dancing.

indicators.note: verbalised means put into speech, so the word is the one said out loud

parts.note: roads are ways for travel

explanation.surface: Routes around an island described in words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Reference a couple of pages, then conclude with nine

to conclude is to end
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Instructions for citing a source: two pages, then finish with the ninth.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is a supplementary reference section at the back of a book.

indicators.note: reportedly says this is how the word is heard when spoken

parts.note: plain means unattractive in looks

explanation.surface: Gossip says some aviator is not good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is an aircraft, something that flies.

clue.text: Feeling of irritation in suit, chafing

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A rough suit rubs and irritates the wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is an irritating sensation on the skin that makes one want to scratch.

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a part is a component or constituent

explanation.surface: Collaring a voter in one's own district.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap is to catch, as with a snare.

indicators.note: back says the letters of a and the promenade word are read backwards

parts.note: the Mall is a London promenade, and a mall is a walk lined with trees

explanation.surface: An animal being walked along a promenade and then back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses A MALL; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal of the camel family.

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the following words are arranged in an odd new way

explanation.surface: Odd nude artworks that critics do not rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrated has not been given a value or assessed.

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Rocks lying dry inside a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is the definition, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in is to be fashionable or popular, the same as being trendy.

clue.text: Diggers loading ship with stuff heading for Estonia

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
to pad is to stuff or fill

indicators.note: heading for says take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Excavators being loaded onto a ship bound for Estonia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diggers' suggests machines or people, but here it means hand tools.
